title: Adaptive execution-path advisor for heterogeneous GPUs and variable-length inference
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight online advisor that selects the best low-level execution path for each inference request based on a compact fingerprint of (hardware architecture, timestamped sequence-length histogram, kv-cache hit hint, and token distribution quantiles). The advisor must run with microsecond-scale decision latency, be resilient to noisy measurements, support safe rollouts, and provide an offline training pipeline to update cost models. Goal: reduce p99 latency for mixed workloads by 10-25% and decrease cost-per-token by enabling cheaper kernels when appropriate without regressions in tail latency.
acceptance_criteria: Advisor introduces <500us median overhead per decision on CPU hot path and <1% additional tail on p99 inference time when enabled
Measured end-to-end p99 improvement >=10% on mixed short/long production trace compared to baseline static policy
Automated fallback: if selected path has 2x observed latency increase within 5 minutes, traffic routed to safe default automatically
Canary rollout framework: support traffic-split, regret-tracking, and automatic rollback hooks configured via Console
Offline retraining pipeline reproducibly produces new cost models from stored microbenchmarks and production traces with unit tests and CI coverage
decision_log: 2025-02-10: Decided on two-layer decision model: a cheap fingerprint-based routing model (bloom of arch+hist quantiles) for the fast path, and a periodic microprobe sampler that updates a lightweight online cost estimator.
2025-02-12: Chose quantile-based encoding (5 quantiles + histogram sketch) instead of raw sequence-length buckets to reduce state size and make the advisor robust to distribution drift.
2025-02-14: Rejected heavy neural cost models due to inference overhead; will use ridge regression with L2 + online exponential smoothing for adaptivity.

2025-02-18: Safety policy approved: require 3 consecutive microprobe rounds with statistically significant improvement before switching away from default for >=10% traffic share; immediate rollback on 2x latency spike.
2025-02-19: Agreed to surface advisor decisions and counters in Console per-model dashboard and add a per-request annotation header for debugging (X-Runtime-Exec-Path).
experiment_results: Microbench harness (NVIDIA A100, Ampere) with 1k micro-batches: cheap-path selection reduced median token latency by 18% on short sequences (<64) and had no measurable regression on long sequences when combined with periodic microprobes.
Heterogeneous cluster test: on mixed hw pool (A100, H100, V100 emulation) advisor reduced cross-host variance; p99 improved by 12% and p995 improved by 6% relative to static selection.

Cost simulation using historical request traces: enabling advisor with conservative rollout reduced simulated token cost by 9% for the embeddings-heavy workload and 6% for chat workload; worst-case hourly rollback occurred once during stress run and triggered safe fallback as expected.

Overhead profiling: decision path accounts for ~220us median CPU time in our Go runtime hook; optimization targets include moving fingerprint encoding to vectorized C and caching per-conn fingerprints to reduce repeated work.
Open question: microprobe frequency vs. stability trade-off — early tuning shows 1 probe per 10k requests balances exploration and stability for most customers but is workload dependent.
